Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union–China Agreement for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (Loi du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et au financement du terrorisme), as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the register of beneficial owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 implementing EU Directive (EU) 2018/843 and subsequent amendments.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport / identity document of each manager, shareholder and UBO (certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or competent authority in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the issuing state is a 1961 Hague Apostille Convention contracting party), otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / criminal record extract of each manager and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or police authority in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each UBO and manager (e.g., utility bill or recent bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified sworn translation; Apostille where the document is public or notarized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming business relationship, reputation and source of initial capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn translation; notarial certification and Apostille if required by the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and register extract for any corporate shareholder / UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against all EU Council restrictive measures and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Lists (including UN-sanctioned persons and entities), the Luxembourg domestic sanctions/asset-freeze lists established by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the FATF high-risk jurisdictions list, and, for USD-sensitive transactions, the OFAC SDN List. Politically exposed persons (PEP) must be identified using the EU AMLD5/FATF definition encompassing senior political office holders, their family members and close associates. Positive hits require immediate filing of a suspicious transaction report with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier – CRF) and refusal or suspension of the contemplated incorporation relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) via www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be distinguishable and not misleading. They may be written using Latin-script characters in any language; however, the official filing with the RCS must provide a French or German transliteration/version where the name is not in one of these languages. The mandatory legal suffix for Société à Responsabilité Limitée is 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are not automatically extended; a new reservation request must be submitted after the 30-day window if incorporation is not completed. Upon rejection by the RCS, the applicant may file a motivated administrative appeal with the Minister of Justice within 15 days of notification (recours hiérarchique). If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may bring an annulment action before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of the rejection decision. Further appeal may be lodged with the Administrative Court of Appeal (Cour administrative). Professional counsel should be engaged before re-submission to avoid identical refusal grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permitted as a registered office for a Luxembourg SARL. A physical Luxembourg address is mandatory. A licensed domiciliation agent may provide the registered office and mail handling services, but the company must maintain adequate commercial substance through board decisions, duly kept accounting records, and executory management in Luxembourg. Purely virtual remote operations without physical infrastructure will not satisfy the statutory registered-office and substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 10% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the initial three-year operating period for a standard low-risk online retail SARL. The probability rises materially where AML/CFT red flags are raised, tax compliance anomalies are identified, or authorities seek verification of substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Formal name reservation and availability search (Luxembourg Business Registers)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR tariff for name check and clearance certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of articles of association (statuts) and constitutive deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration in Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and filing of G01 declaration
Publication of incorporation notice in RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
UBO declaration filing with Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
Registered office / domiciliation service by licensed provider (annual physical address fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for e-commerce SARL domiciliation with mail handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents (3 doc bundles)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent national authorities and consulates in countries of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention per-document fee and consular fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO piercing and AML/CFT screening support (flat fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg-qualified law firm / AML compliance advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee for standard SARL pre-incorporation compliance package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (LSC), Articles 180-1 et seq. (SARL), together with the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on the right of establishment; registration is administered through the Luxembourg Business Registers framework.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and coordinated articles (statuts coordonnés), electronically filed with the RCS by the supervising Luxembourg notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum capital for a SARL, fully subscribed and paid-up before registration. In practice, the funds are deposited on a blocked account (compte bloqué) opened with a Luxembourg credit institution in the SARL's name and released only upon presentation of the RCS registration extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the SARL's issued share capital of twelve thousand euros (€12,000), comprising twelve thousand registered shares with a par value of one euro each, is taken up in full by the sole founding shareholder and is fully paid-up in cash. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office is established at [Registered Office Address] in the City of Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, until lawfully changed by the managers. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the first manager(s) [Name(s)] is/are appointed with sole signature power, effective immediately, to implement the RCS registration, to open bank and payment-processing accounts, to obtain the establishment authorization, and to comply with all filing and governance obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) name search via LBR/Guichet; Luxembourg notary for drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary RCS name availability search through the Luxembourg Business Registers portal. Instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare final draft consolidated articles (statuts coordonnés), choose the registered office address, define the corporate purpose limited to online retail of 3D printers and consumables, and confirm the identity of the first manager(s).
required_dossiers: Two preferred corporate names
Identity documents of founding shareholder and proposed first manager(s)
Registered office lease or notarized landlord consent
Draft corporate purpose in ISIC 4791 scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to identity or distinctive-character conflict, the notary submits an alternative name. If the registered-office consent is deficient, obtain a fresh notarized landlord consent before deed execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital blocking and corporate bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution with notary oversight
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional SARL account in the future corporate name, deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital as a cash contribution, and obtain a capital-blocking certificate from the bank addressed to the notary, confirming that the funds are irrevocably blocked and released only upon presentation of the RCS registration extract.
required_dossiers: Application form and KYC questionnaire for the future SARL
Passport or ID of beneficial owner/founder
Corporate name reservation certificate
Source-of-funds evidence for the capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC/AML queries, provide a banker's reference or transaction breakdown; if refusal persists, select an alternative Luxembourg credit institution while preserving the notary schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the deed of incorporation and first governance resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholder or attorney-in-fact executes the notarial deed containing the SARL's articles, registered office adoption, acceptance of share subscription, appointment of first manager(s), and the adopted first resolution annexed to the deed. The notary verifies identity and capital payment.
required_dossiers: Final draft statuts approved by all parties
Capital blocking certificate from the bank
Original passports and, if applicable, powers of attorney
Registered office address and lease confirmation
Signed first shareholder/managerial resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any shareholder document is incomplete or requires legalization, the notary coordinates a second execution before a Luxembourg notary within 48 hours; any legal flaw is cured by rectificatory deed before RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS e-filing desk, Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or corporate counsel electronically files the notarial deed and coordinated statutes with the RCS through the Luxembourg Business Registers e-filing interface, together with statutory corporate governance declarations. Pay the RCS registration fee and obtain an acknowledgement of deposit.
required_dossiers: Signed notarial deed of incorporation
Coordinated statutes (statuts coordonnés)
Capital blocking certificate
RCS fee payment confirmation
Manager(s) acceptance of office and residency documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or informal observation, counsel responds within the statutory cure period, files a restorative declaration or amended deed, and re-submits electronically.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS inscription, corporate registration extract, and RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS registers the SARL, obtain the official RCS extract and company matricule number, and confirm automatic publication of a legal notice in the electronic official gazette by the registrar. This certificate is the central proof of corporate existence for banks, VAT, and licensing.
required_dossiers: RCS filing receipt or acknowledgement
Notarial deed reference
Payment confirmation of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the extract contains an error in the corporate name, object, registered address, or manager data, file a rectification application with LBR immediately; retroactive correction may be made by registrar discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Guichet unique.lu), Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours, and Inspection du Travail et des Mines
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online application for the right of establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) for the SARL's managers, and simultaneously apply for any municipal, fire, structural, and occupational clearances for the registered office and warehouse, including fire-safety certification and ITM workplace inspection where staff are employed.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extract)
Identity/residency cards and criminal-record certificate of the manager(s)
Lease contract and floor plan for office/warehouse
Fire-safety assessment and any CGDIS clearance
ITM workplace evaluation for employed staff, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authorization is refused, file a written appeal with the Minister of the Economy within two weeks and thereafter with the Administrative Tribunal; supplementary documentation cures most evidentiary deficiencies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des PME et de l'Entreprenariat (Guichet unique.lu), assisted by the Administration de l'environnement for environmental registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement pour le commerce en ligne d'imprimantes 3D, de filaments et de résines d'impression

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report; low-tier environmental registration may be required if uncured resin storage exceeds the de minimis threshold of approximately 100 litres of classified irritant liquids under Luxembourg and EU environmental law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater discharge; any interior drain must be connected to the municipal sewer under a pre-treatment agreement if resin cleanup liquids are disposed of. VOC emissions must remain below the solvent-registration threshold; uncured resin waste and contaminated packaging must be handled as hazardous waste and collected by an authorized Luxembourg waste operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for the warehouse/office; structural load confirmation by a Luxembourg civil engineer where racking or large inventory is installed; and an occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering electrical equipment, ventilation for resin fumes, and manual handling protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties (www.aed.public.lu); Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax (www.impotsdirects.public.lu); unified electronic portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet; official company registry and corporate identification: lbr.lu (Luxembourg Business Registers).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Luxembourg SARL: (1) notarize the articles of association and register the company in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) through the notary and the lbr.lu/eJustice platform; the RCSL assigns the 13-digit national business registration number (matricule). (2) File the RBE beneficial-ownership declaration (see rbe.guichet.lu) within one month of incorporation. (3) Apply to the AEDT for a VAT identification number by lodging Form 630 (VAT registration application) together with the RCSL extract, articles of association and identity documents of the legal representatives; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT number (N° TVA LU) within approximately one to three weeks. (4) The ACD thereafter attributes the corporate income tax reference number (LIP) and municipal business tax reference for CIT and net wealth tax purposes. (5) A foreign seller without a Luxembourg establishment engaged in distance selling into Luxembourg must register for Luxembourg VAT via MyGuichet; a non-EU vendor is domestically required to appoint an accredited Luxembourg fiscal representative unless the OSS/IOSS special schemes apply. (6) If the SARL makes intra-EU distance sales of goods or receives imported goods for onward sale, the seller should activate the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) or Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) modules on guichet.lu for pan-EU VAT compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Luxembourg SARL is an opaque, non-transparent resident company. It is fully subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT, 17% headline rate, effective rate approx. 24.94% in Luxembourg City including the solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax), net wealth tax (0.5% on net assets) and municipal business tax. It is not eligible for pass-through or look-through treatment, and its worldwide profits are taxable under Luxembourg law. Tax transparency is exclusively available to other vehicle forms (e.g., SCS or SCSp partnerships), not to a SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not administer an elective check-the-box classification regime. Statutory filings and elections available to a SARL include: (i) an opt-in fiscal tax unity (integration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR, available where a resident parent holds at least 95% of the share capital of resident subsidiaries, allowing group loss offset and tax consolidation for CIT and municipal business tax; (ii) the participation exemption regime (Article 166 LIR), which operates by statutory eligibility and requires an annual domestic proof of compliance (10% or EUR 6 million acquisition cost holding, one-year holding period, and the anti-abuse substance requirements); (iii) the IP box election (Article 50bis LIR) granting an 80% deduction of qualifying IP income after the application for the regime; (iv) the SPF election for a family wealth-management company opting into the alternative tax regime (Société de Gestion de Patrimoine Familial); and (v) a binding advance tax ruling issued by the ACD Ruling Commission to confirm hybrid mismatch consequences, though the ATAD 1/2 anti-hybrid rules (Articles 168bis to 168sexies LIR) apply mandatorily and no one-tier transparency election is available for a SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) — Luxembourg's broad-based VAT levied under the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC, implemented through the consolidated Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi TVA of 12 February 1979, as amended), administered by the AEDT and identified by the Luxembourg VAT number (N° TVA LU).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Resident businesses: EUR 0 — no general turnover registration threshold applies; a Luxembourg SARL must register for VAT from the first taxable transaction regardless of turnover. Domestic micro-businesses may elect the small-business franchise only where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000 (pre-VAT), which forfeits input VAT recovery. Intra-EU distance sales of goods by a Luxembourg seller are effectively taxable at destination once aggregate annual distance-sales turnover exceeds EUR 10,000; sales at or below that threshold remain subject to Luxembourg VAT unless the seller opts for OSS. Non-established foreign sellers have no Luxembourg VAT exemption threshold and must register for Luxembourg VAT or avail of the OSS/IOSS special schemes for distance sales and imports of goods valued at or below EUR 150.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no mandatory B2B or B2C electronic invoicing and no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), API transmission, or digital stamping obligation. Electronic invoicing is permitted permissively under PEPPOL/UBL formats. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies where suppliers deliver invoices to Luxembourg central public administrations, requiring structured e-invoices (EN 16931/PEPPOL) in the public procurement environment. Luxembourg VAT returns (Form 106) and EU recapitulative statements (ESL) are filed electronically through MyGuichet. Under the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) proposals, standardised e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting may become mandatory for cross-border supplies from the 2027-2028 horizon, but no domestic e-invoicing decree is currently operative.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 40 of the Luxembourg VAT Law zero-rates supplies of goods physically exported outside the European Union by the supplier or a third party acting on its behalf. The following objective criteria must be met to claim 0% export VAT: (i) the 3D printers, resin filaments or consumables are physically dispatched to a non-EU destination within the applicable dispatch deadlines; (ii) the export is evidenced by a valid customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document / LUCAS electronic export message) showing the Luxembourg supplier as exporter and goods released for exit from the EU; (iii) the supplier retains commercial transport documents (Bill of Lading, CMR waybill, Air Waybill, courier manifests) proving the goods have left the Union; (iv) the supplies are recorded in the Luxembourg VAT return (as zero-rated) and the export evidence is maintained for inspection. Intra-EU B2B dispatches to VAT-registered customers in another Member State are likewise exempt subject to production of a valid EU VAT number and ESL reporting. B2C online sales to EU consumers exceeding the EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold are not zero-rated at export but are taxed in the destination Member State via OSS. Ancillary services directly connected to the export (e.g., freight and delivery charges) also qualify for zero-rating under Article 40(2)(b) of the VAT Law.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / LUCAS electronic export message) containing the MRN (Movement Reference Number) and customs release status
Transport document evidencing physical movement out of the EU: Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or Air Waybill / international courier shipment manifest (DHL, FedEx, UPS)
Commercial invoice, packing list and weight list corresponding exactly to the export declaration
Proof of arrival and foreign receipt: foreign customs entry document, signed Proof of Delivery (POD), or logistics carrier track-and-trace report confirming non-EU destination
Foreign exchange settlement evidence: inward remittance certificate (SWIFT MT103, bank credit advice) or Stripe/Shopify payout settlement records received from the overseas purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT applies risk-based, documentary audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims. Where export conditions are not properly evidenced, the supply is retrospectively re-assessed at the Luxembourg standard VAT rate (16%), with the VAT becoming immediately payable together with statutory late-payment interest and administrative surcharges. Misdeclaration of VAT is punishable by fines of up to EUR 3,000 per infraction under Articles 24-25 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; belated filing penalties (EUR 1,500 per instance and a 10% surcharge on the assessed VAT) may also be imposed. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims constitute VAT fraud (Steuerhinterziehung / fraude fiscale) and expose the legal representatives and directors to criminal sanctions including imprisonment of up to five years and/or fines of up to EUR 250,000 in aggravated cases, as well as personal joint tax liability of the directors under general enforcement rules. Input VAT previously recovered may be clawed back along with the re-assessed output VAT, and the applicable statutory limitation period is extended to up to seven years in cases involving evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), as Luxembourg's Eurosystem national central bank; no separate foreign-exchange administration exists and the CSSF is the competent banking-sector supervisor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has no general foreign-exchange control legislation. The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Capital Movements Code. Trade payments, royalties, loan repayments, equity subscriptions and profit remittances do not require BCL or government approval. Practical restrictions are limited to SARL corporate-law distribution tests, 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax where treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief is not available, and bank-level AML/KYC/source-of-funds documentation. For online retail of 3D printers and consumables, non-resident shareholders may remit profits freely once audited/approved accounts show sufficient distributable reserves and the paying bank has verified ultimate beneficial ownership and tax residence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and Eurosystem law impose no statutory time limit for repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio to euro, and no surrender obligation for export proceeds. Export receivables from e-commerce sales may be held indefinitely in foreign currency or converted at commercial market rates. Resident enterprises only have statistical balance-of-payments reporting duties to BCL/ECB under applicable Eurostat rules; this is informational and does not affect convertibility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse de l'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) / Spuerkeess

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: High with conditions. A fintech EMI is viable if it is licensed or registered by the CSSF as an electronic-money institution in Luxembourg or is passporting an EU/EEA e-money licence under Directive 2009/110/EC and PSD2. Global PSPs used by the project, including Stripe and Shopify Payments, are acceptable for customer receipt collection and settlement. Legal constraints are material: an EMI may not take deposits from the public, must safeguard client funds in segregated accounts, and must have a complete Luxembourg/EU AML/KYC/CTF framework. Unlicensed non-EU EMIs servicing Luxembourg residents without a passport are not viable and may be treated as unauthorised payment services. The recommended treasury architecture is to collect via the PSP/EMI rail and then sweep EUR to the Tier-1 Luxembourg commercial-bank settlement account for all material disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not mandate a universal physical domicile test for bank onboarding, but CSSF AML/KYC rules oblige banks to identify and verify directors, senior managing officials and ultimate beneficial owners. In practice, Tier-1 commercial banks require a physical onboarding interview for non-resident directors/UBOs, conducted at the bank's premises or before a Luxembourg notary, or a CSSF-approved remote video/digital identity verification where the customer risk profile is low and the bank's internal policy permits it. For an SARL e-commerce business, the safest route is to instruct a licensed fiduciary/PFS, appoint local substance advisors, and, if requested, bring the ultimate shareholders/directors to one physical meeting in Luxembourg. Remote-only opening exists but is bank-specific and not a legal entitlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk card-acquirer settlements from Stripe/Shopify Payments arrive in aggregated amounts without item-level customer counterparty identification, creating a mismatch with normal invoice-level KYC expectations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce treasury file containing merchant agreement, daily settlement reconciliation reports, transaction-level sales order logs, invoice register, delivery/courier tracking data, returns/refund policy, VAT returns, and confirmation of PCI-DSS-compliant payment processing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership chain includes holding vehicles or jurisdictions that Luxembourg AML risk mapping treats as high-risk or opaque, increasing UBO identification difficulty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transparent ownership chain dossier: certified articles of association, Luxembourg RBE UBO extract, entity structure diagram, certified passport copies, tax residence certificates, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files, professional references, and board resolutions explaining the commercial purpose of each holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Luxembourg substance indicators are weak, raising bank concern that the SARL is a brass-plate vehicle created for tax or regulatory avoidance rather than an active online retail company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance and operational dossier: registered office lease, local administration/accounting services agreement, local director employment or director services contract, board meeting minutes, website operational evidence, customer-support processes, inventory and fulfilment flow explanation, financial forecasts and business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The supply chain involves desktop 3D printers, resin filaments and related consumables that may trigger EU dual-use or proliferation-finance screening for export-control-sensitive technical parameters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade compliance dossier: product technical datasheets, EU Combined Nomenclature classification, dual-use classification assessment under Regulation (EU) 2021/821, end-user/end-use statements for B2B customers, restricted-party screening output, distributor KYC, and written policies excluding sales to embargoed destinations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro injections from EU/EEA shareholders and SWIFT MT103 for non-EU or non-euro injections. The wire narrative must state the exact economic purpose, such as 'Subscription price for SARL shares' or 'Shareholder loan disbursement', and the remitter must be the actual shareholder/lender. The Luxembourg bank will apply an appropriate balance-of-payments statistical code for direct investment/debt claim and will require a board/shareholders' resolution, subscription agreement, notarised articles or capital-increase deed, RCS extract, and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth evidence. For initial incorporation, the notary requires the minimum capital to be deposited in a blocked/escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution before signature; the bank issues an attestation de blocage. Subsequent capital injections should be kept separate from trade receivables in the ledger and formally recorded in the Luxembourg commercial register where the share capital is increased.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Intra-EU for EU suppliers, and SWIFT MT103 or MT103 gpi for non-EU suppliers, including in Field 70 the invoice number, Incoterms, purchase-order number and clear trade purpose. For large or strategic inventory purchases, use a documentary letter of credit issued via MT700 under ICC UCP 600 or documentary collection DP/DA to secure payment. Customer settlement from Stripe and Shopify Payments should be swept into the main EUR treasury account at a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank. Every outbound disbursement must be supported by purchase order, supplier invoice, incoterm evidence, packing list, bill of lading/AWB/courier receipt, customs declaration and pre-screening of the beneficiary against EU sanctions and restricted-party lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD deliverable forward contracts, including flexible forwards, executed with a CSSF-regulated bank or MiFID investment firm under a documented SARL treasury policy.
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP or EUR/CNH FX swaps for short-term liquidity matching and trade payable roll-over.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps, primarily EUR/USD, for hedging long-term shareholder loans or acquisition financing.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies where deliverable settlement capability is limited, used strictly as trade-hedge instruments.
European-style vanilla EUR/USD call and put options for contingent exposure management, with no net speculative position permitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers and publication in RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year-end; for calendar-year accounts by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing measures at the request of any interested third party; fines for directors and managers up to EUR 10,000; repeated non-filing results in default notice and ex officio administrative strike-off of the SARL from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data in the beneficial owners register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 15 March following the reference calendar year; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership filed within one month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 500 to EUR 10,000 and up to six months imprisonment for officers and managers found to have intentionally omitted or falsely declared UBO data; repeated failure may lead to additional RBE registration penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) together with supporting tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, filing must be completed by 31 December of the following year; extensions may be granted upon reasoned request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment by the tax authorities; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 for non-filing or inaccurate filing; potential criminal sanctions for willful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax declaration (impôt sur la fortune) for commercial companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the corporate income tax return, standard deadline 31 December following the tax year; assessment notice then issues within the administrative cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Minimum annual net wealth tax of EUR 1,000 remains payable despite losses; late declaration attracts penalties and interest at statutory rates; persistent non-payment may lead to enforced collection through seizure of assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint a certified independent auditor approved by the CSSF if it exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds on the balance sheet date for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average number of employees above 25. An audit is also mandatory for certain regulated activities, public undertakings, and where the company forms part of a larger group subject to consolidated audit requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP in conformity with the EU Accounting Directive (2013/34/EU). IFRS as adopted by the European Union is permitted for consolidated financial statements and, under specific conditions, may be voluntarily applied to individual annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must annually confirm the complete and current identity of all beneficial owners via the RBE online portal. The confirmation window runs from 1 January to 15 March of each calendar year. Any change in shareholding, ownership percentages, or beneficial interest must be reported within one month of the underlying act or transfer. The registered manager must retain legible documentary evidence of the entire ownership structure, including powers of attorney, corporate diagrams, and individual identity documentation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 – USD 2,800 per year for licensed domiciliation and registered-agent services in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 – USD 14,000 for a certified statutory audit of a small to mid-sized online retail SARL if the mandatory thresholds are exceeded; USD 2,000 – USD 3,500 for a voluntary limited review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg City rate (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge, being 7% of CIT, + 6.75% municipal business tax). A reduced CIT band of 15% applies to the first EUR 175,000 of taxable income, producing a combined rate of 22.80% for that tranche.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains where the SARL holds a direct participation of at least 10% (or with an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1,200,000) for an uninterrupted 12-month holding period. Innovation/IP Box (Art. 50ter LIR): 80% exemption of qualifying net IP/innovation income, yielding an effective combined rate of approximately 4.99%. No general statutory tax holiday; small companies benefit from progressive CIT bands.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1002 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune) filed through the official Luxembourg e-filing channel (MyGuichet / Administration des contributions directes electronic portal). A transfer pricing annex and participation exemption annex are submitted together with the return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a SARL with a 31 December fiscal year-end, the Form 1002 must be filed by 31 December of the immediately following tax year (i.e., up to 12 months after the balance sheet date). The tax administration may grant extensions upon justified request; taxpayers may also be summoned individually to file by a specific date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 13-digit Luxembourg national taxpayer identification number assigned to the SARL at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and foreign branch operations must quote the Luxembourg NIF of the PE or of the local withholding agent; the SARL itself files as a full resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) number and legal form code for a Société à Responsabilité Limitée.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State '20250' type SARL; non-resident managers or shareholders must provide their foreign registration details in the annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Stated accounting period; Luxembourg tax law requires the return to cover a 12-month period unless a special business reason exists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a foreign parent closes accounts on a non-calendar date, the Luxembourg return must still reconcile the Luxembourg statutory year to the group reporting calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross assets per the Luxembourg statutory annual accounts, used for net wealth tax and corporate substance screening.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Luxembourg situs assets; intercompany receivables from the foreign parent must be fully disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial book result (accounting profit or loss) before tax adjustments, as shown in the approved annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Luxembourg-source operating revenues are taxable for a non-resident seller; the resident SARL reports its worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments converting accounting profit to taxable income: hidden profit distributions, non-deductible expenses, excessive management fees, and transaction recharacterizations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Rebilling of group e-commerce costs must be supported by written agreements and arm's-length benchmarking; otherwise ACD may readjust.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends/principal gains derived from qualifying holdings under Art. 166 LIR; requires proof of 10% holding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost and 12-month holding period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent receiving Luxembourg dividends must substantiate treaty or EU directive status via the annuity form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year losses available under Art. 114 LIR; Luxembourg grants a maximum 17-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward follows the Luxembourg entity only; it cannot be used by a foreign head office, and ownership/activity changes may trigger challenge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Net taxable income / ICC base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable base allocated between corporate income tax and municipal business tax; communal allocation is based on payroll and fixed assets in Luxembourg communes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A single-commune SARL files the Luxembourg City allocation; foreign e-commerce sales without local dependent agent do not create an extra communale tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory declaration of cross-border related-party transactions, including purchases of 3D printers/resin filaments, management fees, and financing; Local File must be attached when aggregate controlled transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annex must identify each related counterparty, the transaction amount, the transfer pricing method, and a functional profile; failure to attach the file is independently penalized.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment trigger monthly arrears interest of 0.85% (10.2% per annum) on unpaid taxes, a 10% late-payment surcharge where tax is not remitted by the statutory due date, coercive fines for non-compliance with a filing summons, and separate administrative penalties up to EUR 25,000 for incomplete or non-submitted returns. Criminal exposure for deliberate non-filing is a fine up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under Art. 396 AO.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic dividend withholding tax on distributions by a Luxembourg SARL to its shareholders, whether resident or non-resident; the lower withholding rate of 15% applies without a filing requirement for the distributing company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke 0% relief under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a double tax agreement, the non-resident corporate shareholder must: (i) hold a qualifying participation (generally at least 10%, or the lower treaty threshold) and where applicable maintain the 12-month minimum holding period; (ii) obtain a valid tax residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) from its own tax authority; (iii) deliver the certificate and a properly completed ACD form via the Luxembourg fiscal agent or MyGuichet to the Administration des contributions directes; (iv) obtain prior authorization for reduced or zero withholding before the dividend payment, or alternatively reclaim the excess withholding after payment. The payer must retain the supporting documentation in the SARL transfer pricing and tax file. Failure to obtain authorization results in the full 15% statutory withholding, recoverable only through the treaty refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% for arm's-length interest and royalties paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-resident corporate recipients under domestic law; no significant Luxembourg withholding obligation on ordinary trade debt interest or IP licence fees. Treaty rates generally range 0-10% for interest and 0-5% for royalties where the payee is resident in a treaty country. Anti-abuse: 15% withholding applies to certain payments characterized as disguised dividends, excessive related-party interest, and directors' fees; the ATAD GAAR may override domestic exemptions in artificial schemes.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in a tax year forces the SARL to prepare and maintain a Luxembourg Local File demonstrating arm's-length pricing; a Master File is required for groups whose consolidated turnover reaches EUR 750,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue exceeding EUR 750,000,000. Even below the EUR 1,000,000 threshold, the ACD may request contemporaneous documentation when there is a risk of profit shifting.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a separate offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the OECD/Harmful Tax Practices framework, the ATAD GAAR, and the settled case-law application of the abuse-of-law doctrine require real economic presence. A qualifying e-commerce SARL must maintain: a genuine registered office, local books and records, local personnel with decision-making or management functions, physical or contractual infrastructure (warehouse, fulfillment, supplier contracts), and a business purpose aligned with its actual online retail activities. A 'letterbox' entity generating only passive reseller margins without local activity is exposed to re-domestication, denial of treaty/directive benefits, and reclassification of its Luxembourg residence to the jurisdiction of central management and control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or falsification of the Form 1002, under-declaration of online retail turnover from 3D printer sales, fabrication of supplier invoices, creation of fictitious costs, and hidden dividend extraction disguised as management fees or loan repayments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative: monthly arrears interest at 0.85%, 10% late-payment surcharge, and civil reassessment. Criminal: under Art. 396 Luxembourg General Tax Law, a fine of up to EUR 125,000 per offence and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years for fraudulent evasion; in aggravated cases the fine may be doubled, and seizure of corporate assets including bank accounts and payment-rail reserves (Stripe/Shopify balances) is authorized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant (manager) is personally liable for restitution of unpaid taxes, interest, and penalties where fraud or gross misconduct is proven; personal assets may be seized. Criminal courts may impose an interdiction of professional duties and a travel ban (interdiction de sortie du territoire); imprisonment up to 5 years applies. Piercing the corporate veil follows under Art. 523 of the Law on Commercial Companies for abuse of corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining only a postal address and a nominated agent, with the foreign parent performing all actual e-commerce operations, holding the inventory, contracts, and decision-making outside Luxembourg; arranging circular intercompany invoices to manufacture a taxable margin; utilizing the SARL as a pure conduit for foreign-owned online retail profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax consequences: full re-assessments under the ATAD GAAR and Luxembourg abuse-of-law doctrines, disallowance of all artificial deductions, recharacterization of conduit payments as distributions subject to 15% withholding tax, denial of treaty benefits and of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, and possible determination that the SARL's place of effective management lies abroad, triggering terminal tax on deemed asset disposals and additional net wealth tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and shareholder-directors who approve sham arrangements face personal joinder of tax liabilities, civil liability for distributions paid out of artificial profits, and criminal sanctions for complicity in tax fraud, including fines and imprisonment; the commercial register may strike the company, allowing the ACD to collect from the gérant personally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file and continuously update beneficial owners in the Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), absence of AML policies despite operating high-volume e-commerce payment rails (Stripe, Shopify Payments), concealed identity of the ultimate beneficial owner, and acceptance of undeclared or crypto-linked payments for 3D printer consumables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RBE violations: administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 for a legal person and EUR 1,000 per day of persistence under the Law of 13 January 2019. AML/CTF: fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Luxembourg Criminal Code for money laundering; payment service providers may terminate the Stripe/Shopify merchant account and freeze residual balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable to the SARL and regulators for breach of the beneficial ownership and AML duties; criminal conviction triggers directorial disqualification, asset freezes, and restraint orders. A travel ban may be applied to prevent flight in serious money-laundering proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Improper Benchmarking
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing intercompany purchase prices for 3D printers and filaments at arbitrary levels causing Luxembourg continuous losses, paying inflated royalties to a low-tax group financing entity, failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File documentation when related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000, or applying year-end unilateral margin adjustments without benchmark data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment by the ACD under Art. 56 LIR and OECD rules to an arm's-length outcome, imposition of undeclared dividend treatment on the upward adjustment with 15% withholding tax, monthly 0.85% interest, a 10% penalty on reassessed taxes, and a specific documentation penalty of 20% of the additional assessment when the Local/Master File has not been produced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers who sign incorrectly benchmarked returns and TP documentation are jointly responsible for the reassessed tax where the company cannot pay; personal exposure includes civil damages payable to the ACD, disqualification from management, and criminal liability if the mispricing is found to be a deliberate fraudulent scheme. A Deemed-dividend assessment can be recovered personally where the gérant authorized the artificial intercompany margin.
